findings.summary: CODEX-04-C at 63f913d (base d7e800f) meets all three card criteria within the local synthetic scope. The original words and the immutable receipt/+86400s due time are shown next to the separate current question and founder interpretation in the parent F06 detail and the founder O02 detail. The server enforces exact parent agreement before a founder can accept an alternative; a replaced proposal or a correction clears that agreement. Decline, cancel and every response are labelled delivered:false and never called delivered. Late status keeps the breach against the original deadline, a separate revised estimate that must be future canonical UTC, a DRAFT update marked sent=false, and the cancel route. A persisted intake pause blocks only fresh bookings (eligibility ineligible, submit no_capacity, no receipt); saved-only capture, same-key replay and existing acceptance are unaffected. AcceptRequest returns exactly the common 1.1.0 result. Accept reserves the existing hold once through kernel.apply, including after trial expiry under DECISION-033. Pre-ready decline/cancel releases the claim and the mapped booking once. Every transaction locks the household before consent and domain rows. Facts are AES-GCM encrypted in a hash-chained journal that is reopened and checked before ACK. Each ACK also re-checks current founder/parent authority, so a withdrawal before or during append suppresses the ACK. Founder authority is checked inside the transaction (role, enabled, exact token hash, revocation, expiry). Checks reported: 111/111 tests, build, all 12 protected probes, the unchanged 27-diagnostic/32-line baseline (global tsc still fails; not claimed), 76 route identities and the private build scans. CUA: all eight scenarios ran on 9152a40. The only later browser-source change is a one-line HTTP mapping in adult-http.mjs, and the affected intake journey was re-run at 63f913d. I judge this carry-over sufficient. Reading coverage, all read in full through EOF: root AGENTS, GOVERNANCE, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH and approved/APPROVALS; the exported PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.96 (1321 lines); engineering v1.2 README, ENGINEERING_DESIGN_V1 (411 lines), MODULE_GUIDE and REVIEW_NOTES; PRODUCT_V1 v0.4.1, PRODUCT_DECISIONS and WORK_MODULES v0.3; the CODEX-04-C card; 00-B CONTRACTS v1.1.1 (318 lines); 00-C SCREEN_CONTRACT_MAP v1.0; queue_profile and queue_instructions; the 04-B acceptance notes; LOOP-POLICY-001; INPUT_MANIFEST, SPEC, FULL_COMMIT_LOG, ACTUAL_CHECKS_AND_CUA; FULL_DIFF (2441 lines); and the 9152a40 CUA needs-changes record. Gaps: I could not recompute any SHA-256 (no shell), so the manifest and architecture digests are cited, not verified. I did not separately open the 2cc6fcb CUA record, queue_probe.mjs source or authorizations.json. Every diff file is inside the 15-path grant plus controller metadata. Remaining findings are minor or nit only.

findings.title: Founder queue rows omit receipt/original due time
findings.problem: 00-C O02 specifies queue rows showing receipt, original due, age, status, booked capacity and allowance category. Each founder list row shows only position, state label, breach flag and original words. Receipt and original due appear only after selecting a request. Card criterion 1 ('original wonder/due time remains visible... throughout queue') is met in the detail views, but triage from the list cannot see the 24-hour clock or slack.
findings.fix_check: Founder list rows render the original receipt and original due time (or the remaining slack against the original due) next to the original words, and the founder DOM test asserts this.

findings.title: Paused-intake reason not shown to parent; deviation only disclosed
findings.problem: queue_instructions line 19 requires fresh eligibility to return ineligible 'with a safe intake_paused reason'. The HTTP boundary removes the reason to keep the strict production-client contract, so the parent sees only a generic 'not currently eligible' message and no paused/founder-absence explanation (F01/F04 'temporarily paused'). Enforcement is correct and fails closed. The conflict between the two instructions is disclosed, not resolved.
findings.fix_check: Either a later authorized revision of the production client contract exposes a safe paused explanation, or the report records this as a carried UX gap for the owning module. No new result status is added.

findings.title: REQUEST_QUEUE_CONTRACT.md seam text is stale after 63f913d
findings.problem: Integration limit 1 still says the paused-eligibility client/service seam is unresolved and that the controller must resolve it. The header still says revision2 was not executed. 63f913d resolved the seam with an HTTP mapping, and the checks have since run. AGENTS.md requires accurate records; the contract doc now disagrees with the source and REPORT.
findings.fix_check: The contract doc describes the exact HTTP mapping (ineligible+intake_paused becomes status-only at /adult/production/eligibility) and current verification status, with history preserved.

findings.title: Adult-session validation duplicated outside adult-access
findings.problem: When migration 012 is present, production-submission no longer uses access.withSession. It uses withProductionQueueSession, which reimplements the session checks (throttle lock, enabled account, revocation, issued/expiry) with the production clock so that the intake lock comes before the household lock. The checks are currently equivalent and are even re-checked after work. However, adult-session policy now has two implementations, and future adult-access changes such as idle timeout or rotation would not reach the production path.
findings.fix_check: Session validation is factored or shared so both paths use one implementation, or a test asserts parity between the two paths (expired, revoked, disabled, wrong household).

findings.title: No pre-deadline at-risk indicator in founder queue
findings.problem: PD-013 and WM-04 04-C call for a due-time warning and pre-deadline alerting where possible. The founder queue flags only an actual breach and offers an 'overdue' filter. Warning thresholds are gated under G-E05, so no specific threshold should be invented. Even so, there is no neutral time-to-original-due display that lets the founder act before a breach.
findings.fix_check: The founder detail and list show time remaining to the ORIGINAL due time without choosing a policy threshold, or the gap is explicitly recorded as carried to the owning scheduler/WM-11 gate.

findings.title: Accepted protected files reflowed into long single lines
findings.problem: adult-http.mjs, loop-auth.mjs, family-space.mjs and production-submission.mjs were collapsed from multi-line code into very long one-line statements, alongside the small functional changes. Tests and probes show behaviour is preserved, but the reformat hides the real semantic changes (intake hooks, household-first lock, queue routes) and makes future review and blame harder.
findings.fix_check: Future edits keep the original formatting of accepted files so that diffs isolate the functional changes.

findings.title: Controller status JSON is stale
findings.problem: The status file says state 'blocked' with result_commit pointing at the base d7e800f, which contradicts the appended REPORT evidence at 63f913d. It is controller-managed metadata, but a stale pointer could mis-pin acceptance (compare REVIEW_NOTES finding 8).
findings.fix_check: The controller updates state/result_commit to the exact reviewed head before recording delegated acceptance.
